prompt_text: My roof has hail damage in Denver. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you specific, vetted roofing companies in Denver — but to pick the best local options I need your neighborhood or ZIP code so I can target companies that actually serve your area and have current reviews/certifications.

In the meantime, here’s a short, practical plan and the exact kinds of companies you should call (and why):

1) Call 3 local, manufacturer‑certified roofers (examples: GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT, Owens Corning Preferred). Why: manufacturer‑certified contractors meet training/insurance standards and are more likely to install warranty‑eligible work after hail damage.

2) Call 1–2 storm‑damage specialists / restoration companies that handle insurance claims (e.g., local hail/storm crews or national restoration firms with Denver offices). Why: they’re experienced documenting hail damage, working with adjusters, and can speed the insurance process.

3) Call your insurance company’s recommended contractors (if they provide any), but don’t rely only on them. Why: they’ll be familiar with your insurer’s claim process — but you still want independent estimates.

4) If damage looks extensive or you’re being pressured, call a public adjuster for one inspection. Why: they advocate for policyholders and can help maximize your claim payout (they charge a fee or percentage, so weigh the benefit).

What I’ll need from you to produce a short list of specific companies:
- Your ZIP code or neighborhood in Denver
- Any preferences (local-only, national firms ok, prefer family-owned, etc.)

Also — immediate checklist for the calls/appointments:
- Take clear photos of roof from ground and of downspouts, gutters, vehicles, siding, and any interior leaks.
- Ask each contractor: Are you licensed/insured in Colorado? Do you carry general liability and workers’ comp? Are you a manufacturer‑certified installer (which brands)? Do you handle insurance documentation and meet with adjuster? Do you provide a written estimate and scope of work? What warranties do you offer (materials vs workmanship)?
- Get 3 written estimates and compare line items (tear-off vs overlay, materials, ventilation, drip edge, ice/water shield, permit costs).
- Don’t sign anything the day they show up under “storm special” pressure — get it in writing and confirm timelines and payment schedule.

If you share your ZIP code, I’ll return a short list (3–6) of reputable Denver roofing companies — with why to call each (certifications, storm/insurance experience, specialties, and contact tips).
